name: Anu
role: Sky god and second king in heaven in the Kumarbi succession
fun_fact: Anu's name is the Sumerian word for heaven, and in the Hurrian song he is overthrown by the cup-bearer he had raised.

name: Kumarbi
role: Hurrian father of the gods and deposed king in heaven
fun_fact: Kumarbi is called father of the gods even though the Song of Kumarbi makes him pregnant with Teshub rather than his father.

name: Teshub
role: Hurrian storm god and king of the gods
fun_fact: Teshub's sacred city was Kummiya, and his wife Hebat, brother Tasmisu and sister Shaushka appear with him throughout the Kumarbi songs.

name: Ullikummi
role: Stone giant made by Kumarbi to destroy Teshub
fun_fact: His name means 'Destroy Kumme!', after Kummiya, the city of Teshub that he was made to overthrow.

name: Illuyanka
role: Serpent who fights the storm god in the Purulli myth
fun_fact: The Illuyanka myth was recited at the Purulli festival, and two different versions of the fight survive.

name: Telipinu
role: Vegetation god whose disappearance stops the world
fun_fact: Telipinu's name is probably Hattic, meaning something like 'exalted son', and several Hittite kings took it as a throne name.

name: Hannahanna
role: Mother goddess who searches for the vanished god
fun_fact: Hannahanna's name means 'grandmother', and it is her bee that finds Telipinu asleep in the meadow.

name: Inara
role: Goddess who traps the serpent Illuyanka
fun_fact: Inara bargains with the mortal Hupasiya for his help and later settles him in a house on a rock, warning him not to look out of the window.

name: Hupasiya
role: Mortal helper of Inara in the Illuyanka myth
fun_fact: Hupasiya agrees to help Inara only if she sleeps with him, then ties up the drunken serpent for Teshub to kill.

name: Appu
role: Rich childless man in the Hittite tale of two sons
fun_fact: Appu's sons are named Idalu and Handanza, Hittite words for evil and good, and their quarrel ends in a lawsuit before the Sun God.
